results.title: What is .NET? What You Need to Know Before Migrating from .NET Framework
results.content:
Microsoft’s .NET 5 was released on 10 November 2020 and had some major changes compared to .NET Framework. Since then, there have been several releases every year. The latest version, .NET 10, arrived in November 2025.

If you plan to migrate to the current .NET (.NET 5 to .NET 10) from .NET Framework in the near future, this article will help you prepare for this inevitable migration and avoid the last-minute, unexpected problems that will come up if you procrastinate. [...] .NET is almost a complete reimagining of the old .NET Framework. In fact, .NET is the first major update since the 2016 release of .NET Core. Both .NET Core and Framework were maintained in parallel, allowing you to choose between one or the other, leveraging .NET Standard to make shared libraries between the two. [...] A big change that started from the release of .NET 5 is that Microsoft intends to release a major version every November, with only an even-numbered .NET version after 5 (6, 8, etc.) containing long-term support (LTS). Because of this, you’ll need to plan for regular updates to your code as part of ongoing maintenance.

Some essential .NET Framework features are being transitioned to end-of-life, requiring you to plan to migrate your applications to newer .NET versions.

results.title: Medium
results.content:
.NET releases a new major version every November. Versions with even numbers, like .NET 8 and .NET 10, are Long-Term Support (LTS), meaning they’re supported for a longer time. Odd-numbered versions, such as .NET 9, are Standard Term Support (STS), which means they have a shorter support period.

This post is structured version-wise (8 → 9 → 10), with clear sections on:

### .NET 8: Solid LTS Foundations (Nov 2023) [...] ### Summary

.NET 8 laid a strong LTS foundation emphasizing performance and productivity. .NET 9 focused on SDK evolution, AI building blocks, cloud-native support, and performance tuning. .NET 10 solidifies these with deeper runtime enhancements, C# 14 language upgrades, stronger cloud observability, and future-proof cryptography and DevOps workflows.
